items.stem: A small factory makes screws A and screws B. Each unit of screws A needs 4 hours on machine M₁ and 2 hours on machine M₂; each unit of screws B needs 3 hours on M₁ and 2 hours on M₂. M₁ and M₂ are available for at most 21 and 50 hours a day. The profit is ₹75 per unit of screws A and ₹40 per unit of screws B. Formulate the linear programming problem to maximise profit.
items.answer: Maximise Z = 75x + 40y subject to 4x + 3y ≤ 21, 2x + 2y ≤ 50, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (x, y = units of screws A, screws B)
items.markingKey: Decision variables; objective function; constraints including non-negativity.

items.stem: A dietician wants a mixture of pulse mix and Food X. One kg of pulse mix contains 3 units of vitamin A and 6 units of vitamin C; one kg of Food X contains 3 units of vitamin A and 3 units of vitamin C. The mixture must contain at least 36 units of vitamin A and 32 units of vitamin C. pulse mix costs ₹20/kg and Food X costs ₹15/kg. Formulate the LPP to minimise cost.
items.answer: Minimise Z = 20x + 15y subject to 3x + 3y ≥ 36, 6x + 3y ≥ 32, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0
items.markingKey: Variables x, y = kg of each food (1 mark); objective (1 mark); constraints (1 mark).

items.stem: A cottage industry in Nagpur makes souvenirs of type A (x units) and souvenirs of type B (y units) per week. Each souvenir of type A takes 4 hours of labour and each souvenir of type B takes 2 hours; at most 33 labour hours are available. The store can hold at most 16 units in all. Profits are ₹50 and ₹25 per unit. (i) Write the objective function. (ii) Write all the constraints. (iii) Is (x, y) = (1, 1) a feasible point? Justify.
items.answer: (i) Maximise Z = 50x + 25y (ii) 4x + 2y ≤ 33, x + y ≤ 16, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (iii) Yes: 6 ≤ 33 and 2 ≤ 16
items.markingKey: (i) 1 mark (ii) 2 marks (iii) 1 mark.

items.stem: A jewellery workshop makes necklaces and bracelets. Each unit of necklaces needs 4 hours on machine M₁ and 4 hours on machine M₂; each unit of bracelets needs 3 hours on M₁ and 6 hours on M₂. M₁ and M₂ are available for at most 60 and 20 hours a day. The profit is ₹80 per unit of necklaces and ₹60 per unit of bracelets. Formulate the linear programming problem to maximise profit.
items.answer: Maximise Z = 80x + 60y subject to 4x + 3y ≤ 60, 4x + 6y ≤ 20, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (x, y = units of necklaces, bracelets)
items.markingKey: Decision variables; objective function; constraints including non-negativity.

items.stem: A toy maker makes toys of type A and toys of type B. items.stem: Explain the difference between a feasible solution and an optimal solution of an LPP.
items.answer: Feasible: satisfies all constraints; optimal: feasible and gives the best value of Z.

items.stem: A dietician wants a mixture of Food Y and Food Q.
